title: Count islands in a grid
summary: Scan a map; each time you step on unexplored land you have found a new island, so chalk all of it before moving on.
goal: Count the separate islands on the map

mapping.formal: Land cells connected up, down, left or right
Flood fill that marks visited land

ladder.name: Map each land cell's island, then de-duplicate
ladder.idea: From every land cell, explore its whole island and record the set of cells; count the distinct sets.

ladder.name: Chalk each island once
ladder.idea: Scan the map. On finding land not yet chalked, count a new island and chalk all connected land with a depth-first flood fill.
ladder.insight: Exploring the same island from each of its cells repeats work. Marking cells as visited means each island is explored exactly once.

transfer.problem: A photo is a grid of pixels. Count the separate blobs of black pixels.
transfer.explanation: Each blob is a connected region; flood-fill each new black pixel's region and count how many fills you start.

selfCheck: Marks land as visited before or as it is explored.
Explores only up, down, left and right.
Counts one island per flood fill started.
